_doc: wb_fix_1 (support-churn-winback-fix-first-w1): the ONE copy + gate file for the 'we fixed the thing you waited on' win-back. Ruling R2 (data/support-churn-winback-fable-c1/report.md, Fable 2026-11-03): NO message goes to a churned user until the thing they waited for is DONE and visible in the system of record - the fix ticket routes it (scripts/route_fix.py), fix_readback.py proves it Seen, and winback_fix_send.py renders this copy only for the users whose fix read back. Six fixed FIX_LINE variants, one per cause class, numbers filled from the read-back; 'other' quotes the human reply already sent in Intercom and is the only free text. Offers stay inside the approved set (R3): WB_M2_MONTH1 / WB_M2_ANNUAL40 are the EXISTING coupons in muso-messaging contracts/email/coupons.json, a Regional Discount user keeps the country coupon, a payment_failed churner gets a restart link and NO coupon. Never Klaviyo, never Jaxsta, never a date we do not hold. template.enabled stays false until Fable GO on the six rendered variants (the PR body carries them); --live also needs /etc/hydra/winback-fix.live. Every dated value lives HERE (data), never as a literal in code: a code literal with a date in it is a CI red with a countdown on it.

template.enabled_note: Flipping this to true (with fable_go_ref) is the Fable GO on the six rendered FIX_LINE variants. Until then winback_fix_send.py refuses to hand a live batch to the sender seat; dry-run rendering still works.
template.fable_go_rule: A set fable_go_ref is only a claim; the approval itself is recorded in its own file under docs/support/copy-gos/ (wb_fix_1-regional-suffix.md is the shape: ref, approved text verbatim, ruling verbatim, seat, date, conditions). tests/test_churn_copy_gos.py fails the build when a set ref has no such file, so neither this GO nor the regional one can be self-granted by an edit to this policy.
template.subject: We fixed the thing you were waiting on
body: You wrote to us about {cause_noun} and we did not get back to you the way we should have. That was on us. It is done now: {fix_line}.
You cancelled your {plan_noun} on {pro_ended_date}. If you want to come back, {offer_line}
If anything about the fix is wrong, reply to this email and a person will answer.

fix_lines._doc: Exactly one FIX_LINE per message, chosen by cause class. {n}/{m}/{platform}/{amount} come from the read-back evidence, never from a guess: a variant whose numbers the read-back cannot fill makes the user INELIGIBLE (R2: no fix -> no message).
fix_lines.credits_not_approved: {n} of your pending credits are now approved and showing on your profile{declined_clause}
fix_lines.proof_sent_no_update: we reviewed the documents you sent and {n} credits are now approved
fix_lines.analytics_stale_wrong: your {platform} numbers have been refreshed and now update on schedule
fix_lines.billing_confusion: the {amount} charge has been refunded to your card

merge_claim_results._doc: The merge_claim_stuck copy has two shapes (report 3.2 splits them with a slash); the read-back decides which is true for THIS user, and neither is ever sent without its Seen outcome row.
merge_claim_results.merge: the duplicate profiles are merged and your credits are on one page now

cause_nouns._doc: The plain-words name of the thing the user waited on, for the opening sentence. Short, no jargon, no internal names.

plan_nouns._doc: How the ended plan is named back to the user, from the store's plan slug family. Anything unmatched uses the default.

offers._doc: R3: the approved set only, no new spend. coupon codes, slugs and redeem_by are the LIVE values in muso-messaging contracts/email/coupons.json (the send-gateway refuses a body whose slug is missing there or whose redeem_by is inside min_days_left, so a copy of them here that drifts is a refused send, not a silent discount). offer_lines are the approved sentences (report 3.2) with the redeem link filled in: a sentence that says 'with this link' MUST carry {offer_url}, and the guards refuse a body that says it without one. A Regional Discount user keeps the country coupon: same link, plus the regional sentence, and the coupon itself is country-keyed so nothing new is minted.

monthly.offer_line: your first month back is $1 with this link: {offer_url} (good until {redeem_by}).

annual.offer_line: a year of Pro is $72 with this link: {offer_url}

payment_failed.offer_line: you can restart with the same plan here: {offer_url} — nothing else changes.

regional_suffix._doc: Regional Discount users keep the coupon they already had (country-keyed, not a new discount). Appended to the cadence offer_line above, and ONLY when requires_fable_go is false or fable_go_ref carries the explicit GO for this sentence: it states a price, and the template-level GO covers the six FIX_LINE variants only. Unset = a Regional Discount user is held with a reason, never sent an unapproved price. With the GO recorded, the sentence still ships only to a user whose country coupon is re-checked AT SEND TIME (scripts/churn/coupons.py): HELD appends it, LAPSED or UNVERIFIED drops it and the message still sends. GO: the Fable driver, single sender seat verify-sla-driver-fable-d2, 2026-11-04T14:18:11Z; the ruling, the approved text and its conditions are recorded verbatim in docs/support/copy-gos/wb_fix_1-regional-suffix.md, which fable_go_evidence names.
regional_suffix.text: Your regional discount still applies, so the price stays the same.

readback._doc: The read-back's attempt budget (firstmate inbox 007): a routed ticket is re-read at these many hours after its PREVIOUS attempt, one interval per attempt, and stops after the last one. It is never auto-ineligible - it stays routed and is reported as readback_exhausted for its owning lane. max_per_run is the per-run ceiling of the hourly job, oldest-due first.

holdout._doc: sha256('muso-holdout:' + <user_id>) % modulus == residue is NEVER messaged by this campaign, so returns are measurable against an untouched control. scripts/churn/model.py holdout() is the implementation (the 'muso-holdout:' prefix is part of the assignment, so changing it reshuffles the control group).

caps._doc: The lane's own ceiling on a batch; the sender seat (verify-sla-driver-fable-d2) still owns the fleet-wide daily cap and the one-message-per-user-per-day rule. Both must pass.

exclusions._doc: R5. Each entry names WHERE the truth lives. 'source: lane' = this lane reads it and holds the user on unreadable (fail closed). 'source: gateway' = the send-gateway enforces it at send time (suppression, unsubscribe, marketing frequency, one-per-day) - the lane delegates and records the delegation rather than duplicating a gate it cannot read.

paying_again.why: back on an active/trialing/past_due subscription: nothing to win back

fraud_watchlist.why: the fraud lens or policies/fraud-watchlist.json names them

open_dispute.why: an open chargeback: never a marketing note

affiliation.why: major label / publisher affiliation: a NAMED human answers, never the automated note

one_per_day.why: one message per user per UTC day, fleet-wide

campaign_once.why: one message per user, ever, from wb_fix_1

no_verified_email.why: no address, or an unconfirmed one: the gateway would drop it after we counted it

promise_patterns: we will (?:follow up|get back|be in touch)
guards._doc: forbidden_names: never name a vendor or a data source (captain rule; 'never Jaxsta'). promise_patterns: the exact family that burned these users (report 0.2 'the same copy cs-health 6 flagged as misdirecting') - a body carrying one is BLOCKED, not rewritten. human_reply_min_words: the 'other' variant only answers a reply that is a real ANSWER, so the WHOLE reply has to reach this many words (report 3.1; wired at readback.intercom_verdict). human_reply_sentence_min_words: the separate floor for the ONE sentence we QUOTE out of that reply, which also has to name the fix (a verb plus an object); render.quote_fix_sentence raises a FIXABLE policy gap, never a terminal ineligible, when no sentence qualifies. A fable_go_ref names an approval that must have its evidence file under docs/support/copy-gos/ (tests/test_churn_copy_gos.py). link_claim: an offer sentence that says 'this link' must carry a muso.ai URL in the body.

paths._doc: Deploy-proof state lives under /var/lib (never /opt/hydra, which the deploy rsync overwrites). Every one is overridable by the flag named, so a test or a dry run can point at a scratch dir.

measured_candidates._doc: The Fable report's measured artifact (325 ids, $5,371 list MRR) is kept in firstmate data, NOT in this repo: it is a snapshot of user ids, not code. --source json reads it so the campaign can be rehearsed against the exact audience the report counted before the nightly store (support_state.py, churn-risk-signal-prevent-p1) ships.

churn_priority._doc: Stage 1 writes the churn priority list here and scripts/credit_review/decide.py READS it: the decider sorts these users to the head of the free segment for windows.paid_priority_days (R4's 'a policy key + a sort change'). A missing or unreadable file changes no ordering.

clickup._doc: The lanes whose owner is a person or the support agents write a hydra-action-request task to the ClickUp User Requests board (901000600160, workspaces/support/skills/action-request/SKILL.md). That board is drained: resolve-notify.py, clickup-todo-dedupe.py and the support agents read it. The credit-review and proof lanes do NOT write a task: their owner is the decider cron, which reads the churn priority file (paths.churn_priority) and already holds these users' open requests. Every task carries the churned:<date> tag, paid priority, and is deduped by its marker before creation.

merge.title: Merge duplicate profiles (churned user, paid priority)

analytics.title: Analytics not updating (churned user, paid priority)

refund.title: Refund/charge fix for a churned paying user (paid priority)

claim.title: Profile claim stuck for a churned paying user (paid priority)

caroline.title: Answer a churned paying user's unanswered thread (paid priority)

sender_seat._doc: R5: the lane NEVER sends. It renders, guards, ledgers, and hands ONE batch manifest to the single sender seat. verify-sla-driver-fable-d2 owns the seat, the fleet daily cap and the template routing; the seat writes the gateway's send.messages row. This lane keeps its own ledger so 'was this user messaged by wb_fix_1' is answerable without the gateway.
